title: Accidental hypothermia (adult)
subject: emergency
summary: Core temperature below 35 degrees C. Handle gently, prevent further heat loss, stage by core temperature or the Swiss system, rewarm actively in moderate to severe cases, and send patients in or at risk of cardiac arrest to an ECPR centre. Below 30 degrees C, limit shocks to 3 and withhold adrenaline.

sections.title: Recognise and stage
items: Accidental hypothermia: unintentional fall in core temperature below 35 degrees C. Primary: cold exposure. Secondary: sepsis, hypoglycaemia, hypothyroidism, adrenal insufficiency, alcohol or sedative intoxication, stroke, trauma, immobile elderly.

Swiss staging when core temperature cannot be measured: I conscious and shivering (35 to 32 degrees C); II impaired consciousness, shivering reduced or absent (32 to 28); III unconscious with vital signs (28 to 24); IV no vital signs (below 24).

Measure core temperature with a low-reading thermometer: oesophageal (lower third) if intubated, epitympanic thermistor otherwise; rectal and bladder probes lag during rewarming. Infrared ear, oral and axillary readings are unreliable.
India: cold-wave exposure in the north and in hills, homeless and elderly people, alcohol intoxication, high-altitude travellers and troops, trauma victims and cold-water immersion.

sections.title: Immediate management
items: Check breathing and pulse for up to 1 minute in an unconscious hypothermic patient (bradycardia and slow shallow breathing are expected); use ECG, capnography or ultrasound if available.
Handle gently and keep horizontal; avoid active limb movement. Cut off wet clothing, insulate with dry blankets, a vapour barrier and head cover, and shield from wind.
Oxygen, bedside glucose, IV access, and defibrillator pads (not just ECG leads) because VF can be triggered by handling.

Transfer directly to a centre able to provide ECPR (VA-ECMO) if in cardiac arrest or at risk of it: heart rate below 45/min, systolic BP below 90 mmHg, ventricular arrhythmia, or core temperature below 30 degrees C.

sections.title: Rewarming by stage
items: Mild (stage I): warm environment, passive and active external rewarming, warm sweet drinks if alert and able to swallow; shivering is useful and should be allowed.

Moderate to severe (II to III): active external rewarming (forced-air blanket, heating pads) with IV fluids warmed to about 40 degrees C; warmed fluids prevent further cooling but do not rewarm on their own.

Failure to rewarm (temperature static or falling, rising lactate, falling consciousness or BP, ventricular arrhythmia): add active internal rewarming (intravascular catheter, CRRT or haemodialysis); use ECLS if circulation is unstable.
Expect hypovolaemia (cold diuresis) and vasodilatation during rewarming: give warmed crystalloid carefully with close monitoring.
Bradycardia, hypotension and atrial fibrillation are physiological in moderate to severe hypothermia and usually resolve with rewarming alone.
Rewarm patients with a circulation to about 37 degrees C; on ECLS for arrest, rewarm at 5 degrees C per hour or slower.

sections.title: Hypothermic cardiac arrest (ERC 2025)
items: Standard CPR at normal rate and ratio. Asystole, fixed dilated pupils, rigidity, unwitnessed arrest and low ETCO2 are NOT reasons to stop. Do not start or stop only for lethal injury, a frozen body, valid DNACPR, rescuer danger, or avalanche burial over 60 minutes with asystole and a blocked airway.

Below 28 degrees C when continuous CPR is impossible (difficult rescue): intermittent CPR, alternating at least 5 minutes of CPR with no more than 5 minutes without; below 20 degrees C, no more than 10 minutes without.
Defibrillation: if VF persists after 3 shocks and core temperature is below 30 degrees C, delay further shocks until above 30 degrees C.

Adrenaline: withhold below 30 degrees C (it accumulates); give 1 mg IV once core temperature reaches 30 degrees C unless ECPR is imminent; at 30 to 35 degrees C give it every 6 to 10 minutes. Standard ALS from 35 degrees C.
Amiodarone: one 300 mg loading dose for a shockable rhythm; delay further doses until core temperature exceeds 30 degrees C.

Use a mechanical CPR device for long transport or difficult terrain. Rewarm with VA-ECMO (preferred over cardiopulmonary bypass); use the HOPE score in hospital to estimate survival with ECLS. If no ECPR centre can be reached within about 6 hours, rewarm with non-ECLS methods during CPR.

sections.title: Monitoring and investigations
items: Continuous ECG, core temperature, BP (arterial line if unstable), SpO2 (often unreliable with vasoconstriction), urine output.

Blood gas analysed at 37 degrees C without temperature correction (alpha-stat), glucose, potassium and electrolytes, lactate, CK, renal function, lipase or amylase, coagulation (hypothermic coagulopathy is under-read because samples are tested at 37 degrees C).
Look for the cause: blood cultures, alcohol and drug screen, TSH and cortisol if suspected, CT head or trauma survey as indicated.
Watch for afterdrop and rescue collapse during extrication or early rewarming, and later for pneumonia, ARDS, pancreatitis, rhabdomyolysis and frostbite.

sections.title: Disposition
items: Admit moderate or severe hypothermia to HDU or ICU. A fit person with mild primary hypothermia can go home once warm, well, eating and returning to a safe environment.
Treat the underlying cause and address social factors (homelessness, alcohol dependence, falls and self-neglect in the elderly).
After ROSC or ECLS rewarming: post-cardiac arrest care; avoid post-resuscitation hyperthermia.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Using a standard thermometer that does not read below 34 to 35 degrees C.
Declaring death in a cold patient before rewarming ('not dead until warm and dead').
Repeated shocks and adrenaline every 3 to 5 minutes below 30 degrees C.
Rough handling or sitting the patient upright, which can trigger VF.
Missing secondary causes such as sepsis, hypoglycaemia or hypothyroidism.

drugs.name: Adrenaline (epinephrine) in hypothermic arrest
drugs.dose: Withhold below 30 degrees C; 1 mg IV once at 30 degrees C; every 6 to 10 minutes at 30 to 35 degrees C; standard 1 mg every 3 to 5 minutes from 35 degrees C

drugs.name: Amiodarone in hypothermic arrest
drugs.dose: 300 mg IV once for a shockable rhythm; further doses only above 30 degrees C

drugs.name: Warmed crystalloid (0.9% saline or balanced)
drugs.dose: Boluses of 250 to 500 mL warmed to about 40 degrees C, titrated to BP and perfusion
drugs.notes: Avoid overload; central venous pressure monitoring helps in severe cases.

drugs.name: Dextrose
drugs.dose: 25 g IV (100 mL of 25% or 50 mL of 50% dextrose) if glucose below 70 mg/dL (3.9 mmol/L)
drugs.notes: Hypoglycaemia is common in alcohol-related and malnourished patients.
